answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may vote on jobs or claim rewards. The protocol caps each stake’s influence and slashes it when a randomly audited task fails, so copying software or minting names creates no extra weight. A raven may spot a reef of linked accounts, but the defense rests on the bond: an attacker must tie up real capital for each identity and risk losing it, while an echo of honest behavior alone earns no voting power.
